originalTitle: Current Ebola outbreak worst ever in DR Congo, WHO says
title: Brave Helpers in Africa: Learning About Ebola
content:
Hello, Africa! A Big News Story

Hi everyone! Your friendly news reporter for Africa is here. Today, we have an important story from a country called DR Congo. DR Congo is a very big and beautiful place in our amazing continent of Africa. Sometimes, tiny, tiny things we can't even see can make people feel sick. These tiny things are called germs. Right now, there is a special kind of sickness called Ebola that is making some people in DR Congo unwell.

What is Ebola?

Ebola is caused by a very tiny, invisible bug. We call this bug a virus. These little virus bugs are so small, you need a special super-powerful microscope to see them! When the Ebola virus bug gets inside a person's body, it can make them feel very sick. People might get a high fever, which means their body gets very, very hot. They might also feel super tired, have a tummy ache, or feel very weak. It's like having a very bad flu, but much, much worse. People who get Ebola need a lot of help from doctors and nurses to try and get better.

A Very Big Sickness in DR Congo

Right now, many people in DR Congo have caught the Ebola virus bug. The grown-ups at a big health group called the World Health Organization say this is a very, very big sickness for DR Congo. They have never seen so many people get sick with this kind of Ebola in this country before. This means lots and lots of doctors, nurses, and health helpers are working extra hard there right now. **Did you know?** The World Health Organization (WHO) is like a big team of smart doctors and health helpers from all over the world. They work together to help keep everyone healthy and safe from sicknesses!

How Do People Get Sick with Ebola?

Ebola is not like a cold or a cough that spreads easily when someone sneezes near you. You cannot get Ebola just by sitting in the same room as someone. People get sick with Ebola when they touch the blood or other body liquids from someone who is very, very sick. This could be sweat, spit, or other liquids from a person who has the Ebola bug inside them. That is why doctors and nurses wear very special protective clothes. These clothes help keep them safe while they are helping people who are sick. **Did you know?** Washing your hands with soap and water for as long as it takes to sing "Happy Birthday" twice is one of the best ways to keep tiny germs away! It's like magic for your hands!

Brave Doctors and Nurses are Heroes!

There are many brave doctors, nurses, and health workers in DR Congo right now. They are like real-life superheroes, but without capes! They are working tirelessly, day and night. These brave helpers wear special suits that cover them from head to toe. These suits include gloves, masks, and special eye protectors. The suits might look a little bit funny, but they are very important. These special suits keep the doctors and nurses safe from the Ebola bug. They can then take care of the people who are sick, giving them water, comforting them, and trying their very best to make them feel a little better. **Did you know?** Health workers sometimes have to spend many, many hours in their special protective suits. It can get very hot and tiring inside, but they do it because they care so much about helping others!

What is a Vaccine? What is a Treatment?

Sometimes, we get a tiny shot, called a vaccine, to stop us from getting sick in the first place. A vaccine is like a shield for your body. It teaches your body how to fight off germs before you even meet them! For this kind of Ebola, there isn't a *fully approved* vaccine for everyone to get yet. But scientists are working very, very hard and testing new ones to find the best shield possible! A treatment is like special medicine that helps you get better when you are already sick. Right now, there isn't one special medicine that cures Ebola completely for everyone. But doctors give people other medicines to help with their fever, pain, and to keep their bodies strong. Scientists and doctors are working super, super hard every single day to find new shields and new medicines to fight Ebola! **Did you know?** Scientists all over the world work together like detectives to find cures and ways to stop sicknesses. They are like super-smart puzzle solvers for health!

What is a "Strain"?

You know how there are different kinds of fruits, like red apples and green apples? Well, there can be different kinds of tiny bugs too, even if they are all called Ebola. This Ebola bug is a special "strain." It's like a particular type or version of the Ebola virus. This particular strain is making many people very sick in DR Congo. But people are working hard to understand this special strain and find the best ways to stop it from spreading and to help those who are sick. **Did you know?** DR Congo is famous for its beautiful green forests and amazing animals, like gorillas and chimpanzees! It's a country full of life and natural wonders.

How Can We Help?

Even if we are far away, we can still help in simple ways! We can learn about Ebola and share true information with our friends and family. We can make sure to wash our hands often with soap and water to stay healthy ourselves. This helps keep all kinds of germs away. We can send good thoughts to the people in DR Congo and to all the brave health helpers. We can also be kind and caring to everyone around us. When we are kind, we help make the world a happier and healthier place for everyone, everywhere.

Looking to the Future with Hope

It's a big challenge to stop Ebola, but people are not giving up. Doctors, nurses, and scientists are working tirelessly to help. They are trying their best to stop the Ebola bug from spreading to more people. They are also trying to find the very best ways to help people get well and strong again. With so many smart and kind people working together, we can all hope that things will get better soon. Africa is strong, and the people of DR Congo are strong too. Let's all hope for a healthy and happy future for everyone!
summary: Brave doctors and nurses are working very hard in DR Congo, Africa, to help many people who are sick with a serious illness called Ebola, while scientists search for new medicines and vaccines.
whyMatters: This matters because a lot of people are getting sick in DR Congo, and it's important for everyone to stay safe and for doctors and scientists to find ways to help them get better.

originalTitle: Spain's PM blames traffickers after 60,000 migrants reach Ceuta from Morocco
title: A Big Journey: Friends Across the Water!
content:
Hello, amazing friends from all over our beautiful continent, Africa! It’s your friendly news reporter, here to share a story about courage, journeys, and helping hands. This story comes from a special part of Africa, where it almost touches another continent called Europe!

A Special City Called Ceuta

Imagine a city that is part of one country, but it's physically stuck onto another country! That's a bit like Ceuta. Ceuta is a city that belongs to Spain (which is in Europe), but it’s actually right on the map of North Africa. It sits right next to Morocco, which is a country in Africa that many of us know. Think of it like a special doorway. On one side, you have the big, warm lands of Africa, and on the other side, just a little bit of water or a fence, you have Europe. It’s a very interesting place because it shows us how close we are to our neighbours, even across seas and borders!

Many People on a Journey

Recently, a lot, a lot, a lot of people made a big journey to Ceuta. We are talking about maybe as many children as would fill hundreds of schools! It was around 60,000 people. Can you imagine that many people traveling together? They came from Morocco and other parts of Africa, walking and even swimming in the big ocean water, to reach Ceuta. Why did they make such a long and sometimes difficult journey? Well, just like all of us, these people want good things for their families. They wanted to find a place where life might be a little bit easier, where there might be more food, better schools for children, or safe jobs for grown-ups. Everyone wants to feel safe and have a chance to be happy, right? They had hopes and dreams in their hearts, just like you and me. They were looking for a chance to build a better life for themselves and their loved ones. It takes a lot of bravery to leave your home and go on such a big adventure.

Why Do People Travel So Far?

Sometimes, in different parts of the world, things can be very difficult. There might not be enough food, or maybe there are no schools close by, or it’s not safe to stay in their homes. When people face these big problems, they often start looking for a new place where they can live peacefully and grow. This is why people sometimes leave their homes and travel to other countries. It’s not an easy decision to make. Imagine leaving your friends, your toys, and your favourite places! But they do it because they believe there is hope for a brighter future somewhere else. They dream of a place where they can send their children to school every day, where they can find work, and where they can sleep soundly at night without worries. Did you know? Africa is a huge continent with 54 different countries! Each country has its own special stories, cultures, and people, but sometimes, people from one country might need to travel to another looking for help or opportunities.

Helping Hands and Sad Hearts

When so many people arrived in Ceuta, it was a very big surprise for everyone. The people in Ceuta and Spain tried their best to help. They provided food, water, and blankets to those who were tired and hungry from their long journey. It’s important to always be kind and help others when they need it most, isn't it? However, traveling like this can be very difficult and even dangerous. Sometimes, there are grown-ups who are not kind. These people are sometimes called 'traffickers'. They might trick people, making big promises about a wonderful new life, but then make the journey very unsafe and ask for lots of money. They make things hard for everyone. The leader of Spain, called the Prime Minister, was very sad and worried about this. He said these not-so-kind grown-ups who trick people are making things very difficult and dangerous for those just trying to find a better life. He wanted everyone to know that people should be safe when they travel and not be tricked by others.

Coming Home or Finding a New Home

After a little while, many of the people who had traveled to Ceuta decided to go back to Morocco. Maybe they missed their homes, or maybe they realised the journey was too hard for now. It’s okay to go back home when a journey is too much. And for others, brave helpers tried to find them safe places to stay, either in Ceuta or other cities. Every person on this big journey has a story. It teaches us about hope, about difficult times, and about how important it is for people to help each other. It reminds us that no matter where we come from, we all want to be safe, happy, and loved. Did you know? Morocco, the country where many of these people started their journey, is known for its beautiful colourful markets, delicious food, and friendly people!

What Can We Learn?

This story from Ceuta shows us that our world is full of people looking for good things. We can all learn to be kind, to understand that sometimes people have to make very big choices, and to always, always offer a helping hand when we can. Every child, every person, deserves a safe home and a chance to be happy. Let’s remember to be kind to everyone, no matter where they come from, because we are all part of one big global family. And that's your news from Africa for today! Stay curious and keep being kind!
